title: HIPAA, BAAs and zero data retention for Claude
titleVi: HIPAA, BAA và chính sách không lưu giữ dữ liệu cho Claude

units.text: Ensure compliance with regulations
What you will be able to do
Say who processes prompts and outputs on each Claude surface, and what that means for which controls apply
Tell what zero data retention covers and what it leaves out, and explain why the API does not block ineligible features under it
Enable HIPAA readiness, predict which requests the API will reject, and keep PHI where the BAA protects it
Decide where a PHI workflow can legally run, and let one ZDR workspace use a Covered Model without changing the others
Key concept
Data processor

The party that handles your prompts and outputs depends on where you run Claude. On the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry, that party is Anthropic. On Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform, it is the cloud provider. Anthropic's retention arrangements and BAA only reach data that Anthropic processes.
In this lesson
Who processes the data decides which controls apply

Who processes the data decides which controls apply

Every compliance question about Claude starts with the same fact: who processes the data in this deployment. On the Claude API (api.anthropic.com), Claude Platform on AWS and Claude in Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic processes prompts and outputs. That means Anthropic's two data handling arrangements, zero data retention (ZDR) and HIPAA readiness, are the controls you request and configure. On Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform, the cloud provider is the processor, and the equivalent controls are in that provider's own retention and compliance documentation.

Claude Platform on AWS is the surface people most often get wrong. It is billed through AWS Marketplace and opened from the AWS Console, but Anthropic operates it and it follows the same data retention policy as the first-party API. On Bedrock, AWS runs inference. If you put a deployment in the wrong column, you will read the wrong vendor's compliance terms for it.

Some commitments apply even without either arrangement. Retained data is never used for model training without your express permission. Conversation content is not retained by default. The exception is
Covered Models
, which require 30-day retention. Where a feature has to store something, its own page gives the retention period.
Checkpoint 1 of 8
Check yourself

A team buys Claude through AWS Marketplace and opens it from the AWS Console as Claude Platform on AWS. Their compliance officer asks which vendor's data retention controls govern their prompts and outputs. What is the correct answer?
Both together: AWS controls the prompts sent from its console, and Anthropic controls the outputs Claude generates.
The same vendor as for Amazon Bedrock, because both run Claude on AWS infrastructure and AWS performs inference for both.
Anthropic, because Anthropic operates Claude Platform on AWS and processes the data, so the first-party API's retention policy and Anthropic's arrangements such as ZDR apply.
AWS, because the service is billed through AWS Marketplace and opened from the AWS Console, so AWS's retention and compliance documentation applies.
Sources
Zero data retention: its scope, and the requests it does not stop
Under ZDR, Anthropic does not store your prompts or responses at rest once the API response has been returned. You request it from the Anthropic sales team, and it is enabled
per organization
. If you create a second organization under the same account, it does not inherit ZDR. The account team has to enable it there separately.
ZDR applies to:
The Messages and Token Counting APIs, for the features marked eligible in the feature eligibility table
Claude Code used with API keys from a Commercial organization, except for metrics logging: if it is turned on, usage statistics are exempt and may be retained
Claude Platform on AWS, on request through your Anthropic account representative

ZDR does not apply to the Claude Console (including the playground), Claude Managed Agents (session transcripts persist until you delete them), consumer Free, Pro and Max plans, the Claude Teams and Enterprise interfaces, Claude for Excel, or third-party integrations. Claude Code on Claude Enterprise has its own, separate ZDR offering. CORS is not supported for ZDR organizations, so browser apps have to send their calls through a backend proxy.
Predict first
An organization under ZDR sends a /v1/messages request that uses code execution, a feature marked "No" for ZDR. What does the API do?
Rejects it with a 400 error, because the feature is not eligible
Accepts it but strips the code execution tool before running the request
Accepts it, and the code execution data falls under that feature's own retention policy

ZDR is a promise about storage, not a filter on requests. Features marked "No" are usually stateful: they store jobs, files or container state, so they cannot be zero-retention. The API still accepts them, so nothing stops a developer from adding code execution to a ZDR workload. If the workload must stay fully ZDR, your own review process has to catch that, because the API will not.
Exam trap
Under ZDR, the API rejects requests that use non-eligible features, just as it does under HIPAA readiness.
Why is that wrong?
Checkpoint 2 of 8
Check yourself
Your company's main organization has ZDR enabled. Which of these workloads is actually covered by it?
Developers running Claude Code with API keys from the ZDR Commercial organization, with metrics logging turned off
A second organization, newly created under the same account, calling the Messages API with eligible features
A Claude Managed Agents deployment created by the ZDR organization
Engineers testing prompts in the Claude Console playground while signed in to the ZDR organization
Sources
HIPAA readiness: a BAA plus feature limits the API enforces

HIPAA readiness is the arrangement for organizations that handle protected health information (PHI). It needs a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and a HIPAA-enabled organization. It does not work by deleting data right away. It applies a broader set of safeguards than ZDR: encryption, access controls and audit logging. An organization that processes PHI uses HIPAA readiness and does not also need ZDR.

Most organizations can turn it on themselves. In the Claude Console, go to the Data retention page (platform.claude.com/settings/privacy). Organization admins with the HIPAA management permission see a HIPAA compliance card there. From it, download the BAA and the HIPAA Implementation Guide, then accept the agreement as an authorized legal representative. Your enablement is tied to the exact BAA version you downloaded. The controls apply as soon as you accept, and the setting is
permanent
: an administrator cannot turn it off. Organizations that need a negotiated BAA go through the sales team instead.

Once HIPAA readiness is on, the API enforces the feature list. A request from a HIPAA-enabled organization that includes a non-eligible feature gets a 400 error naming that feature. You remove the feature and send the request again. The error text says "without Zero Data Retention", but that is only the API's wording. Turning on ZDR does not fix the error. One exception: client-side tools whose eligibility entry says they are not blocked are accepted, but they are still outside HIPAA readiness.
The 400 error a HIPAA-enabled organization gets when a request includes a non-eligible feature
json

PHI is protected only in certain places. Message content, attached images and PDFs, and file names or metadata tied to messages are all protected. Workspace names, user details, billing data and support tickets are not expected to contain PHI. JSON schemas are the trap. With structured outputs or
tools, the API compiles each schema into a grammar and caches it separately, without PHI protection. Keep patient details out of property names, enum values, const values and pattern regexes.
How the two arrangements differ for a Claude API organization

Why is that wrong?
Checkpoint 3 of 8
Check yourself

A health-tech startup has just accepted the standard BAA on the Console Data retention page. Their next /v1/messages request returns a 400 invalid_request_error: "The requested features are not available for HIPAA-regulated organizations without Zero Data Retention: code_execution." What should the developer do?
Remove code execution from the request and send it again, because HIPAA readiness blocks features that are not eligible.
Have an administrator turn HIPAA readiness off, send the request, and then turn it back on.
Send the request again unchanged, because the error lasts only until the BAA acceptance has finished processing.
Ask Anthropic sales to enable ZDR as well, because the error says HIPAA organizations need Zero Data Retention to use the feature.
Sources
Where a BAA does and does not cover PHI

A signed BAA does not make every Claude product safe for PHI. It covers only the organization that accepted it, and only the features it lists as eligible. Each of these uses of PHI falls outside it, even when the company has a BAA:
Claude Console.
You can turn on HIPAA readiness from Console settings, but processing PHI in the Console interface, including Workbench, is not covered.
Consumer plans.
Claude Free, Pro and Max are excluded, so clinicians sharing a Pro subscription for chart lookups are outside the agreement.
Claude Enterprise before activation.
Standard Enterprise plans have no BAA coverage until the Primary Owner turns on HIPAA compliance under Data and privacy and accepts the BAA.
Beta features and third-party integrations.
These are generally excluded. For Enterprise Skills and connectors that send data to third parties, administrators who enable them are responsible for how they are used.

For a clinical summarization pipeline, the compliant setup is a dedicated HIPAA-enabled organization that calls the Claude API using only eligible features. The API's 400 errors then stop any ineligible feature from slipping into a request.

Claude Code is not covered under an API organization's HIPAA readiness. It can be covered on a HIPAA-ready Claude Enterprise plan, but only if the Primary Owner applies the HIPAA configuration and developers sign in with their Enterprise account and connect directly to the Claude API. Managed settings make sure that is the only path that works.

With the configuration applied, Claude Code turns off features that would send data elsewhere: WebFetch (web search still works), cloud sessions and Remote Control,

Exam trap
Once the company has a BAA, PHI can go through any Claude surface tied to the same organization, including the Console Workbench or the default Enterprise setup.
Why is that wrong?

Which of these PHI workflows is covered by the hospital group's signed BAA?

Checkpoint 6 of 8
Exam question

A digital health startup wants to route protected health information (PHI) from patient intake forms through Claude to summarize clinical notes. The compliance team confirms Anthropic has signed a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with the company, but must choose where in the Claude product surface this workflow can legally process PHI. Which deployment satisfies the BAA?
A dedicated HIPAA-enabled organization calling the Claude API with only BAA-eligible features enabled
The Claude Console's Workbench interface, since it authenticates through the same organization as the API
A Claude Pro subscription shared among clinical staff for quick ad hoc chart lookups during rounds
The default Claude Enterprise workspace, without activating HIPAA settings under Data & Privacy
Sources
Using a Covered Model inside a ZDR organization

Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 are Covered Models, and they require 30-day data retention. They are not available under ZDR unless Anthropic has expressly authorized it. The API does not quietly switch on retention for you. If a request reaches one of these models from an organization or workspace whose retention setting does not meet the requirement, it fails with a 400 error.
The error a Covered Model request returns when the retention requirement is not met
json

To pilot a Covered Model without dropping ZDR everywhere, use a workspace-level override. On the Console Data retention page, pick the workspace from the dropdown, choose Standard data retention (30-day retention), save, and accept the terms in the confirmation dialog. Retention takes effect only after you accept. After that, Covered Model requests from that workspace succeed, and every workspace without an override stays on the organization's ZDR default. Don't use the Default Workspace for the pilot: it always follows the organization's setting.

Switching to HIPAA readiness is the wrong tool for this. HIPAA readiness is the arrangement for PHI, and it cannot be turned off again. It is not a way to unlock models. On a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan with the HIPAA configuration applied, members can use Covered Models in Claude Code and Cowork under the BAA.
Exam trap
An administrator can trial HIPAA readiness to unlock a model and then switch it off afterwards.
Why is that wrong?
Checkpoint 7 of 8
Put it in order
Put these steps in order to let one team pilot Claude Fable 5.1 while the rest of the ZDR organization stays on zero data retention.
On the Console Data retention page, select the pilot workspace (not the Default Workspace) from the dropdown at the top of the page.
Send Covered Model requests from that workspace and confirm that they succeed, while workspaces without an override stay on ZDR.
Review and accept the data retention terms in the confirmation dialog.
Select Standard data retention (30-day retention) and click Save.
Check order
Checkpoint 8 of 8
Exam question

An engineering organization runs under a zero data retention (ZDR) arrangement. One team wants to pilot a Covered Model that requires 30-day data retention in a single workspace, without changing the ZDR posture of the rest of the organization. What should they do?
Enable 30-day data retention in that workspace's privacy controls while other workspaces remain on ZDR
Ask Anthropic to disable ZDR for the entire organization so every workspace can call the Covered Model
Switch the workspace to the HIPAA-ready arrangement instead of ZDR to unlock the Covered Model
Keep sending requests under ZDR and let the API silently apply 30-day retention to that workspace only
